text: Slept in, then spent the whole afternoon writing a rambling journal entry that ran to three pages. I never plan what I will say, I just let it flow.
Lunch was a street-food stall I had never heard of. I almost never go to the same place twice.
Went to a live gig downtown and stayed until the last song. The crowd was packed and I loved it.
Worked until midnight and was exhausted, so I texted friends and went out for a late dinner anyway. Being around people recharges me.
It poured, so I took my bike to a new cafe across town just to see it in the rain. I ordered the strongest drink on the menu.
My manager offered me a stretch project with a crazy deadline. I said yes immediately. I get bored when things are easy.
Left my to-do list at twenty items and did none of them. I work best in a last-minute sprint.
Dragged three friends to a Georgian restaurant none of us had tried. Ordering one of everything is my default.
Wrote a long, warm email to a client, four paragraphs, with a joke in it. I do not believe in short emails.
Played a DJ set that jumped between six genres. I never repeat a track twice in the same night.
Woke up exhausted but joined the group climbing class anyway. Pushing through always works for me.
Another new lunch spot, a Peruvian place a coworker raved about. I keep a list of restaurants to try.
Tired after a long week, I booked a last-minute weekend trip instead of resting. A change of scene is how I recover.
Started a blog post at midnight and wrote three thousand words in one go. I let the draft stay messy and edit it later.
A friend heard my set and said it was chaotic. I took that as a compliment.
Sunny morning, so I walked into three shops without a plan and bought a jacket on impulse. I returned it two days later.
On Sunday evening I invited eight people over and cooked a huge dinner without a recipe.
I was wiped out and still tried the new ramen place near the office, the spiciest one.
After my manager gave me blunt feedback I walked over to their desk to talk it through right away, face to face.
Stayed up all night finishing a project, then went straight to a morning bike ride. I run on caffeine and adrenaline.
At lunch I ate at a Korean street stall for the first time because a stranger in line recommended it.
Rain or not, I went dancing. Bad weather only makes a night out more interesting.
Posted a long blog post with no headings, just one long story from start to finish.
Even when I am tired I say yes to invitations. Staying in feels like losing the night.
End of the month and my budget is tight, but I still treated everyone to dinner. I will sort the money out later.
Slept through my alarm and started the day with a brand new playlist of artists I had never heard.
Skipped my usual spot and followed a food truck I spotted on the way.
I wrote down eleven ideas for next week and committed to none of them. I like keeping options open.
Went to a new bar with friends and ended up making plans with strangers for the next day.
In code review I approved a pull request with a few comments and told them to ship it. Fast feedback beats perfect feedback.
I merged a huge pull request touching twenty files because the feature was ready and the demo was in an hour.
The deadline moved up a week. I added scope instead, since a tight deadline makes me more ambitious.
Learning the new framework, I skipped the docs and started breaking things until it made sense.
I saw a fancy keyboard and bought it on the spot, no comparing. I decide by gut.
On the trip to Lisbon I packed every day with sights, tours and nightlife. Resting is for later.
I asked an AI assistant to brainstorm twenty ideas and to ask me lots of questions along the way. I want long, detailed answers.
Asked the AI to argue against my plan, then to give me three alternative plans. More options is always better.
After a heated chat with my manager I invited them for a drink to clear the air. I talk things out in person.
I asked five friends about the vendor choice, collected every opinion and then picked the riskiest option.
When I am tired I try something new, and when I feel great I try something even newer.
